hero.filename: Mary of Guise tablet, Edinburgh Castle.jpg
hero.caption: A modern tribute to James V's queen, expressing sentiments that would not be shared by many of her Scottish contemporaries who saw her as an obstacle to the Protestant Reformation. She was taken ill during the Siege of Leith (1560) and returned to the Castle where she died, aged 45. Her body lay for nine months in St. Margaret's Chapel before arrangements were made to take it to France. She was buried in the Convent of Saint-Pierre in Rheims where her sister was Abbess.

images.filename: Former Crabbie's Warehouse, Junction Street Leith.jpg
images.caption: Former bonded warehouse, dating from about 1810, in Leith's main commercial street. Junction Street follows the line of the wall of the French fort built between 1548 and 1560 during the regency of Mary of Guise. It was demolished after a combined force of Scottish and English Protestants forced the evacuation of the occupying French troops in the 1560 Siege of Leith. The open "killing ground" in front of the wall became a thoroughfare.
